complianceRequirements: Stationary CI ICE used in Guam, American Samoa, or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands must meet emission standards in 60.4205 (except non-emergency engines ≥30 liters/cylinder must meet 60.4204(c)).
Stationary CI ICE in Guam, American Samoa, or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands are not required to meet the fuel requirements in 60.4207.
Prior to December 1, 2010, owners/operators of stationary CI engines in areas of Alaska not accessible by the Federal Aid Highway System should refer to 40 CFR part 69 for fuel requirements.
Governor of Alaska may submit an alternative plan for requirements under 40 CFR part 60, subpart IIII, for certain rural public-sector utilities.
Owners/operators of stationary CI ICE using non-diesel fuel, or those authorized under 60.4207(d), may petition for alternative emission standards (with justification).
See Table 8 to subpart IIII for applicability of General Provisions (60.1 - 60.19).
recordKeepingRequirements: Maintain records of annual hours of operation for each emergency generator calculated monthly as the sum of each consecutive 12-month period.
Maintain all fuel supplier certifications with each shipment.
Maintain results of all stack tests, visible emission evaluations and performance evaluations.
Maintain records of scheduled and unscheduled maintenance and operator training.
Records shall be available for inspection by the DEQ and shall be current for the most recent five years.

Maintain records of the occurrence and duration of any bypass, malfunction, shutdown or failure resulting in excess emissions for more than one hour, including date, time, duration, description, corrective action, preventive measures, and name of person generating the record.
Maintain records of all notifications submitted to comply with the subpart and all documentation supporting any notification.
Keep records of maintenance conducted on the engine.
If the stationary CI ICE is a certified engine, retain documentation from the manufacturer indicating certification.
If the stationary CI ICE is not certified, keep documentation showing engine meets the emission standards.

For emergency engines, keep records of engine operation in emergency and non-emergency service as recorded through the non-resettable hour meter; record time of operation and the reason for operation.
If equipped with a diesel particulate filter, keep records of corrective actions taken after high backpressure is indicated.
Records of maintenance and training shall be maintained on site for a period of five years and shall be made available to DEQ personnel upon request.

Owners and operators of non-emergency stationary CI ICE that are greater than 2,237 KW (3,000 HP), or have a displacement >= 10 liters per cylinder, or are pre-2007 model year engines that are greater than 130 KW (175 HP) and not certified, must: (1) submit an initial notification with required engine and owner information, emission control equipment, and fuel used; and (2) keep records of all notifications and supporting documentation, maintenance conducted on the engine, certification documentation if applicable, and documentation that the engine meets the emission standards if not certified.

If the stationary CI internal combustion engine is an emergency stationary internal combustion engine, the owner or operator is not required to submit an initial notification. Starting with the model years in table 5 to this subpart, if the emergency engine does not meet the standards applicable to non-emergency engines in the applicable model year, the owner or operator must keep records of the operation of the engine in emergency and non-emergency service that are recorded through the non-resettable hour meter, including the time of operation and the reason for operation.

If the stationary CI internal combustion engine is equipped with a diesel particulate filter, the owner or operator must keep records of any corrective action taken after notification by the backpressure monitor that the high backpressure limit of the engine is approached.

Owners/operators must keep records of performance test results, engine manufacturer data, and control device vendor data indicating compliance with the standards or conduct and record results of initial performance tests to demonstrate compliance.

You must comply with the labeling requirements in 60.4210(f) and the recordkeeping requirements in 60.4214(b) for new emergency stationary CI ICE beginning in the following model years: 19 KW < 56 (25 HP < 75): 2013; 56 KW < 130 (75 HP < 175): 2012; ≥130 KW (≥175 HP): 2011.
notifications: Notify Director, Piedmont Region in writing within 30 days after the actual date construction of the emergency generators commenced. Notify Director, Piedmont Region in writing of the anticipated start-up date of the emergency generators postmarked not more than 60 days nor less than 30 days prior to such date. Notify Director, Piedmont Region in writing within 15 days after the actual start-up date of the emergency generators. Notify Director, Piedmont Region of malfunctions of the affected facility or related air pollution control equipment that may cause excess emissions for more than one hour, as soon as practicable but no later than four daytime business hours after the malfunction is discovered. Provide a written statement giving all pertinent facts, including the estimated duration of the breakdown, within two weeks of discovery of the malfunction. When the condition causing the failure or malfunction has been corrected and the equipment is again in operation, notify the Director, Piedmont Region.

Owners and operators of certain non-emergency stationary CI ICE must submit an initial notification as required in §60.7(a)(1), which includes owner/operator name and address, facility address, engine information (make, model, family, serial number, model year, max power, displacement), emission control equipment, and fuel used.

Owners and operators of non-emergency stationary CI ICE that are greater than 2,237 KW (3,000 HP), or have a displacement >= 10 liters per cylinder, or are pre-2007 model year engines greater than 130 KW (175 HP) and not certified, must submit an initial notification as required in 60.7(a)(1), including name and address of owner/operator, address of affected source, engine information (make, model, engine family, serial number, model year, maximum engine power, engine displacement), emission control equipment, and fuel used.
Notification and recordkeeping (per 60.7) applies as specified in 60.4214(a).
